groups.label: Rejected: added to the book, made it worse

benchmarks.name: 60/40 stocks and bonds
benchmarks.blurb: 60% SPY and 40% intermediate Treasuries (IEF), rebalanced daily.

cards.name: Trend + Carry
cards.reason: The one book that passed every test. It trades daily on paper.
cards.expected: Trend following and carry are two of the best-documented premia across asset classes, and they tend to pay at different times. A small book of liquid ETFs should capture both.
cards.citation: Hurst, B., Ooi, Y. H. & Pedersen, L. H. (2017). A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing. Journal of Portfolio Management 44(1).

spec.data: About 23 ETFs across stocks, bonds, credit, commodities and currencies, 2007 to 2026
spec.execution: Next-day open, 7 bps a trade
spec.bar: Every component passed the alpha gate on its own before it was added
spec.trials: 33 trials counted in the last change (v42)

cards.why: It works because its parts lose money at different times. Trend makes most of its money in long sell-offs and loses in choppy markets; carry earns a steady premium in calm markets. A small classifier skips the weakest trend entries, and exposure is halved when the S&P is below its 200-day average in a volatile market. None of it predicts returns. The last change sized each trend by its t-statistic instead of its sign, which cut trend turnover by a fifth.
cards.mind: A forward record that falls well below the backtest's 5th-percentile path.
gates: Sharpe vs the book before the change
Deflated Sharpe at the true trial count

diag.title: Return over each crisis window

cards.name: Regime de-risk
cards.reason: Halving exposure in falling, volatile markets halved the worst drawdown.
cards.expected: Trend's worst losses come in sharp equity reversals. We can't predict those, but we can react to them once the market is both below its long-term average and volatile.
cards.citation: Moreira, A. & Muir, T. (2017). Volatility-Managed Portfolios. Journal of Finance 72(4).

spec.data: The meta-labelled book, 2007 to 2026
spec.execution: Rule checked at the close, applied the next day; 7 bps on every change in exposure
spec.bar: Higher Sharpe and a smaller worst drawdown, stable across nearby thresholds

cards.why: The rule is simple: when SPY is below its 200-day average and its 21-day volatility is above 20%, the book runs at half size. It fired in 53 separate episodes over 18 years, so it costs little to run. On the meta book it cut the worst drawdown from −10.5% to −5.4% and lifted Sharpe from 1.22 to 1.25, and the worst drawdown stayed at −5.4% for every nearby threshold we tried.

diag.title: Worst drawdown, native volatility

cards.name: Meta-label filter
cards.reason: A small classifier skips weak trend entries. Bigger models did worse.
cards.expected: Meta-labeling leaves the trading rule alone and trains a model to decide which of its signals to act on. That suits a market where returns are mostly noise.
cards.citation: López de Prado, M. (2018). Advances in Financial Machine Learning. Wiley.

spec.data: Every trend entry, 2007 to 2026, labelled by what happened next
spec.execution: Model retrained walk-forward with purged folds; trades at the next open, 7 bps
spec.bar: Book Sharpe up at the true trial count

cards.why: Out of sample the model is right only a little more often than a coin (AUC 0.54), but dropping the worst-looking entries was enough to lift book Sharpe from 1.04 to 1.23. A depth-2 model beat depth-4 and depth-8 models, because with this little signal a bigger model fits noise.

diag.title: Book Sharpe by model size

cards.name: Trend + Carry base book
cards.reason: The two sleeves blended by risk, with nothing fitted.
cards.expected: Blending two sleeves that rarely lose together should give a higher Sharpe than either alone, without fitting anything to the data.
cards.citation: Bailey, D. & López de Prado, M. (2014). The Deflated Sharpe Ratio. Journal of Portfolio Management 40(5).

spec.data: 2007 to 2026, full ETF universe
spec.execution: Monthly rebalance, next-day open, 7 bps
spec.bar: Bootstrap 5th-percentile Sharpe above 0, stable under one-setting changes, survives crises

cards.why: Trend and carry correlate at +0.13, so the blend is smoother than either sleeve. Changing any one setting kept Sharpe between 0.93 and 1.12, so the result doesn't depend on one lucky parameter. Adding 28 more ETFs lowered Sharpe to 0.93, so the universe stayed small.

diag.title: Sharpe after changing one setting

cards.name: Cross-asset trend
cards.reason: The first idea that worked. It gained 7.1% in 2008.
cards.expected: Assets that have been rising tend to keep rising for a while, across stocks, bonds, commodities and currencies, and the effect has paid in most long sell-offs.
cards.citation: Moskowitz, T., Ooi, Y. H. & Pedersen, L. H. (2012). Time Series Momentum. Journal of Financial Economics 104(2).

spec.data: About 23 ETFs, from 1993 (few existed before 2007)
spec.execution: Monthly rebalance, next-day open, 7 bps
spec.bar: Sharpe above 0.40 and positive in crises

cards.why: Each ETF's position is the average sign of its 3-, 6- and 12-month returns, scaled so every asset carries the same risk. Because it can go short, it gains when a sell-off lasts: +7.1% in 2008 while SPY fell 43.4%. It loses in fast reversals like 2020, which is what the regime de-risk was later built for.

diag.title: Return over each crisis window

cards.name: Carry and defensive sleeve
cards.reason: Steady income in calm markets, where trend struggles.
cards.expected: Assets with a higher yield tend to earn more than their price change suggests. A long-only income book tilted by the yield curve should earn that premium in calm markets.
cards.citation: Koijen, R., Moskowitz, T., Pedersen, L. H. & Vrugt, E. (2018). Carry. Journal of Financial Economics 127(2).

spec.data: Treasury, inflation-linked, credit, gold and real-estate ETFs, from 2003
spec.execution: Monthly rebalance, next-day open, 7 bps
spec.bar: Blend Sharpe between 0.8 and 1.1

cards.why: It holds bonds, credit and gold in risk-parity weights and leans into duration when the gap between 10-year and 3-month yields is wide. On its own it earned a higher Sharpe than trend (0.98 against 0.67), but it has no defence in a long sell-off, and trend does. The two correlate at +0.13. Blended by risk they reached 0.84 over the full window, and 1.03 from 2007, once enough ETFs existed.

diag.title: Sharpe of each sleeve and the blend

cards.name: S&P stock momentum
cards.reason: Sharpe 0.17 after costs, against 0.91 for buy-and-hold.
cards.expected: Stocks that rose most over the past year tend to keep outperforming for a few months. It is the strongest single-stock anomaly on record.
cards.citation: Jegadeesh, N. & Titman, S. (1993). Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers. Journal of Finance 48(1).

spec.data: Point-in-time S&P 500 members, 2013 to 2026, cleaned prices
spec.execution: Monthly rebalance, next-day open, 7 bps
spec.bar: Sharpe above 0.5, set before the run (v27)

cards.why: The anomaly was published in 1993, and our data starts in 2013, two decades after publication, when it is widely traded. Within the S&P 500 the winners and losers are close together, so the spread a monthly rebalance can capture is small next to the cost of turning the book over. An earlier run looked good; that result came from five corrupted price days in 2010 and 2011.
cards.mind: A cleaner, broader universe (small caps) where momentum is less crowded, which free data doesn't cover.

diag.title: Calendar-year return

cards.name: Post-earnings drift
cards.reason: Market beta, not drift: alpha −3.25% a year.
cards.expected: After a large earnings surprise, prices tend to keep drifting the same way for weeks. We traded in the direction of big earnings gaps and held for up to 45 trading days.
cards.citation: Bernard, V. & Thomas, J. (1989). Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift: Delayed Price Response or Risk Premium? Journal of Accounting Research 27.

spec.data: S&P 500 earnings gaps, 2021 to 2026
spec.execution: Entry at the next open after the gap, 7 bps
spec.bar: Sharpe above 0.4 and positive alpha against SPY
spec.trials: 7 S&P sleeve trials in v28 (5 PEAD ablations)

cards.why: Most of its return came from holding stocks while the market rose. Regressed on SPY, it had a beta of 0.36 and an R² of 0.50. After taking out that market exposure, what's left is slightly negative: −3.25% a year, t −1.21. Holding 0.36 of the index would have done better, with fewer trades.

diag.title: Daily return against SPY's, 2021 to 2026
diag.note: About half the trading days are plotted. The line is the regression recorded in the v28 study.

cards.name: S&P short-term reversal
cards.reason: The original engine. It lost money, with a 56% drawdown.
cards.expected: Stocks that fell most over the last few days tend to bounce. This was the engine the project started with, beta-neutral and rebalanced often.
cards.citation: Lehmann, B. (1990). Fads, Martingales, and Market Efficiency. Quarterly Journal of Economics 105(1).

spec.data: Point-in-time S&P 500 members, 2014 to 2026
spec.execution: Next-day open, 7 bps
spec.bar: Sharpe above 0

cards.why: A reversal edge lasts a few days, so the book turns over many times a year, and every turn pays 7 bps on both legs. In the S&P 500, the most heavily traded stocks in the world, the bounce is smaller than that cost. The sleeve lost money (Sharpe −0.08) and fell 56% from its peak.

diag.title: Sharpe, 2014 to 2026

cards.gap: Gross-of-cost Sharpe was never recorded for this sleeve, so the brief's gross-vs-net chart can't be drawn without a rerun.

cards.name: Cointegrated pairs
cards.reason: Uncorrelated with the book, but only the strictest filter made money.
cards.expected: Two stocks whose prices move together should drift back when they separate. The trade is market-neutral by construction, so it should diversify the book.
cards.citation: Gatev, E., Goetzmann, W. & Rouwenhorst, K. G. (2006). Pairs Trading: Performance of a Relative-Value Arbitrage Rule. Review of Financial Studies 19(3).

spec.data: Same-sector S&P 500 pairs, 2013 to 2026
spec.execution: Both legs at the next open, 7 bps a leg
spec.bar: Net Sharpe above 0.40 and correlation with the book below 0.3

cards.why: Its correlation with the book was +0.06, so it would have diversified. The five variants were set before the run, from the loosest rules to the strictest. The four looser ones lost money after costs (Sharpe −0.07 to −0.38). Only the strictest, with a half-life gate and a stable hedge ratio, came out positive: net Sharpe 0.24 with a 41% drawdown. Filtering that hard left almost nothing to trade.

diag.title: Net Sharpe of each pre-set variant, as recorded

cards.gap: The pairs engine never recorded trade counts, so the chart of trades a year against filter strictness can't be drawn. Rerun on today's data, the best variant reproduces; the four looser ones don't.

cards.name: The original "TGA" engine
cards.reason: Its +0.60 Sharpe vanished when the price data was re-downloaded.
cards.expected: Graph-topology and reversal signals on S&P 500 stocks, with a classifier gate and Kelly sizing, could earn a daily edge.
cards.citation: Lo, A. & MacKinlay, A. C. (1990). When Are Contrarian Profits Due to Stock Market Overreaction? Review of Financial Studies 3(2).

spec.data: S&P 500, 2022 to 2026, a 768-ticker copy of the price data
spec.execution: Next-day open, 7 bps
spec.bar: None fixed in advance (this was before the alpha gate)
spec.trials: Not counted (v10 to v24 predate the trial ledger)

cards.compare: The same rules on a fresh copy of the data
cards.why: When the price cache was re-downloaded in May 2026 with 831 tickers instead of 768, every stock's cross-sectional rank moved, and the result moved with it: the base rule went from −0.04 to −0.15. A result that changes with the ticker list is an artifact of the data. v26 then showed the engine's own alpha was indistinguishable from zero; the +0.60 came from its momentum leg.
gates: Same result after the cache change

diag.title: Sharpe of the same rules on two copies of the price data

cards.repro: Not reproducible: the price cache was re-downloaded in May 2026 (768 → 831 tickers), which moved every cross-sectional rank.

cards.name: Before and after the accounting fix
cards.reason: Bugs in our own simulator made four sleeves look good.
cards.expected: Once the S&P book was frozen, pairs, drift and momentum sleeves should add independent return. The first runs said they did.
cards.citation: McLean, R. D. & Pontiff, J. (2016). Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability? Journal of Finance 71(1).

spec.data: S&P 500, 2010 to 2026, two price caches
spec.execution: Next-day open, 7 bps
spec.bar: Momentum above 0.5, drift above 0.4, combined above 0.6 (set in v27)

cards.compare: The same sleeves on clean data
cards.why: Three bugs, found one after another. Short positions were marked as twice the entry price minus the current price, a phantom gain on every short. Short-sale proceeds were counted as buying power, so leverage spiralled. And five corrupted price days in 2010 and 2011 carried momentum's whole result. On clean, single-vintage data momentum fell from 0.54 to 0.17 and the combined book from 0.63 to 0.11.

diag.title: Sharpe before and after the fixes

cards.gap: P&L by cause (the phantom short gain on its own) wasn't saved, so the chart shows each sleeve's Sharpe before and after instead.

cards.name: Currency trend
cards.reason: Sharpe 0.15 on its own, and it lowered the book's.
cards.expected: Trend following works in currencies too, and a currency sleeve should diversify a book that is mostly stocks and bonds.
cards.citation: Moskowitz, T., Ooi, Y. H. & Pedersen, L. H. (2012). Time Series Momentum. Journal of Financial Economics 104(2).

spec.data: Six currency ETFs, 2007 to 2026
spec.execution: Same engine as the book's trend sleeve, next-day open, 7 bps
spec.bar: Net Sharpe above 0.40 and a higher book Sharpe

cards.why: Currency trends have been weak since about 2010, a period when developed-market interest rates sat close together near zero. The best of eight variants earned a Sharpe of 0.15, and its deflated Sharpe was 0. Added to the book as a third sleeve, it took risk budget from two sleeves that earn more, so the book's Sharpe fell.

diag.title: FX trend's Sharpe against the bar

cards.repro: Rerun on today's data (ETF cache 2026-09-11) gives Sharpe 1.020 against the recorded 1.041, outside the 0.02 tolerance, so the curve isn't drawn. The price cache was re-downloaded after this study ran.

cards.name: LSTM features
cards.reason: Its small lift came from look-ahead and vanished walk-forward.
cards.expected: A neural network trained on price histories might learn features the hand-built ones miss, and feed them to the meta-label model.
cards.citation: Hochreiter, S. & Schmidhuber, J. (1997). Long Short-Term Memory. Neural Computation 9(8).

spec.data: 831 S&P 500 price histories for training, the book's ETFs for testing, 2008 to 2026
spec.execution: Same meta-label model and gate as the live book
spec.bar: Book Sharpe up with the network trained only on past data

cards.why: In v36 the network was pretrained once on the whole 2008–2026 history, so a 2010 feature came from a model that had seen 2020. The book's Sharpe rose from 1.226 to 1.242. Retrained at each date on past data only, the lift went away: 1.222, slightly below the book without it. The out-of-sample AUC moved by at most 0.008, inside the noise.

diag.title: Book Sharpe with and without LSTM features
labels: LSTM, trained on all the data

cards.repro: Not redrawn: retraining the walk-forward network stalls on this machine (TensorFlow on Apple silicon), so the card shows the recorded Sharpe ratios instead of a regenerated curve.

cards.name: Calm-market leverage
cards.reason: Levering up in quiet markets cut Sharpe from 1.22 to 0.86.
cards.expected: If the book is safer in calm markets, running it at higher leverage then should raise returns without much extra risk.
cards.citation: Moreira, A. & Muir, T. (2017). Volatility-Managed Portfolios. Journal of Finance 72(4).

spec.data: The meta-labelled book, 2007 to 2026 (June 2026 data)
spec.execution: Leverage set from trailing volatility, applied the next day
spec.bar: Higher Sharpe

cards.why: Calm stretches end suddenly, so the rule was often at its most levered when a sell-off began, and the book took the first days of each sell-off at full size before the rule could react. Cutting exposure after markets turn works; adding it before they do concentrates the tail risk.

diag.title: Book Sharpe

cards.repro: The v39 calm-market test was run in an analysis session whose code and settings weren't saved, so there is no curve to redraw.

cards.name: Stock-bond regime filter
cards.reason: Changed almost nothing: Sharpe +0.008, same drawdown.
cards.expected: The de-risk rule might work better if it only fired when stocks and bonds fall together, the regime in which a book like this is most exposed.
cards.citation: Baltas, N. & Kosowski, R. (2020). Demystifying Time-Series Momentum Strategies: Volatility Estimators, Trading Rules and Pairwise Correlations. SSRN 2140091.

spec.data: The deployed book, 2007 to 2026
spec.execution: Same as the live overlay
spec.bar: Sharpe up 0.03, or turnover down 15%, or drawdown 1 point smaller

cards.why: The extra condition changed the de-risk decision on 110 of 5,815 days (1.9%), because the sell-offs it was meant to pick out were mostly ones the simple rule already caught. Sharpe went from 1.193 to 1.201 and the worst drawdown didn't move, short of every bar. An extra moving part that changes nothing is a cost.
gates: ≥ base + 0.03, or turnover −15%, or drawdown +1 pp

diag.title: Before and after the filter

cards.name: VIX curve inversion trigger
cards.reason: It switched late, re-risked in rebounds, and tripled overlay trading.
cards.expected: When front-month VIX futures trade above the second month, the market is pricing near-term stress. That might be a faster de-risk signal than SPY's trend and volatility.
cards.citation: Cheng, I.-H. (2019). The VIX Premium. Review of Financial Studies 32(1).

spec.data: Our own VIX futures curve from Cboe settlements, the deployed book, 2007 to 2026
spec.execution: Signal at the settle, applied the next day, same de-risk size and lag
spec.bar: Sharpe up, drawdown no worse, every crisis within 1 point, turnover up at most 25%

cards.why: The curve inverts and flips back within days around every volatility spike. So the trigger cut exposure after the first drop and restored it during the rebound, then cut again. It helped a little in fast shocks like 2015 and 2018 and cost 1.3 points in the August 2024 rebound. Sharpe fell from 1.242 to 1.122 and the overlay traded three times as much.

diag.title: Book return over each crisis window

cards.name: Treasury auction pair
cards.reason: Gross return was below cost even before paying for the hedge.
cards.expected: Treasury notes cheapen in the days before a scheduled auction and recover afterwards. A pair hedged with short-term Treasuries should capture the swing.
cards.citation: Lou, D., Yan, H. & Zhang, J. (2013). Anticipated and Repeated Shocks in Liquid Markets. Review of Financial Studies 26(8).

spec.data: 2,793 Treasury note and bond auctions from Treasury's records, IEF and TLT, 2009 to 2026
spec.execution: Opens only, next-day open, 7 bps per unit traded, hedge ratio from the past year
spec.bar: Mean gross return per round trip at least 14 bp to continue, 28 bp to go on

cards.compare: The 14 bp stop and 28 bp go-on bars
cards.why: The swing is there for new issues of long bonds, a few basis points before and after the auction. But TLT moves about six and a half times as much as SHY, so hedging one unit of TLT means trading about fifteen units per round trip: roughly 107 bp of cost against 4 to 14 bp of gross return.
gates: Every auction: gross return per round trip

diag.title: Gross return per round trip, basis points

cards.repro: No single equity curve: auctions overlap, so each trade was scored on its own, per round trip.

cards.name: TLT month-end
cards.reason: Real but small, and the book already holds it.
cards.expected: Bond index funds extend duration at each month-end, and Treasury volume now runs much higher on the last day of the month. Long bonds might earn a premium over those days.
cards.citation: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Liberty Street Economics (2024). End-of-Month Liquidity in the Treasury Market.

spec.data: TLT, 236 month-ends, 2007 to 2026
spec.execution: Buy at the open two days before month-end, sell at the next month's first open, 7 bps a side
spec.bar: Mean gross return per round trip at least 28 bp, and a deflated Sharpe counted against 9,500 calendar rules
spec.trials: 3 for the study, 9,500 for the deflated Sharpe

cards.compare: The live book, already long TLT at 89% of month-ends
cards.why: One day carries it: from the open the day before month-end to the month-end open, TLT averaged +20 bp, and it showed up in IEF, TIP and corporate bonds too, but not in SPY. So the effect looks real. It is about 27 bp a trade on three days a month, costs take half, and the live book is already long TLT at most month-ends. Adding a 10% sleeve moved the book's Sharpe from 1.242 to 1.243, and counted against the 9,500 calendar rules that have been mined, its deflated Sharpe is 0.005.

diag.title: TLT's average open-to-open return by day, basis points
diag.note: L is the month's last trading day and F the next month's first; each bar runs from that day's open to the next day's open.

cards.name: Agriculture curve proxy
cards.reason: Earned what plain momentum earns. Sugar carried it.
cards.expected: In agricultural futures, the change in the curve's slope predicts returns beyond plain momentum. With no free contract-level data, we tested a proxy built from fund prices.
cards.citation: Boons, M. & Prado, M. P. (2019). Basis-Momentum. Journal of Finance 74(1).

spec.data: Corn, soybeans, wheat and sugar futures and funds, 2011 to 2026
spec.execution: One tick a side and two ticks a roll, 8% volatility target
spec.bar: Net Sharpe at least 0.30 and at least 0.10 above 12-month momentum

cards.why: The proxy earned a net Sharpe of 0.21, the same as 12-month momentum on the same markets, and the book already runs a trend sleeve. Its profit came from sugar (97% of it) and soybeans (67%), while wheat lost 61%, so the three grains together added about 2%. There was no grain curve premium to pay for.
cards.mind: The free contract archive holding enough curve history to run the real test, around 2028.

diag.title: Share of profit by market

cards.name: Deep-RL volatility agent
cards.reason: Fed properly, it held almost exactly equal weights.
cards.expected: A reinforcement-learning agent might learn when to shift risk between assets better than a fixed rule.
cards.citation: Schulman, J., Wolski, F., Dhariwal, P., Radford, A. & Klimov, O. (2017). Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms. arXiv 1707.06347.

spec.data: Live paper track, June to October 2026
spec.execution: Daily, through the same paper broker as every strategy
spec.bar: Weights that differ from equal weight in a way that pays

cards.why: For months a data bug starved the agent, so it always fell back to its default. Once fed properly, its weights stayed within 1.7% of equal weight. It had learned that the safest answer is to spread risk evenly, which a one-line rule does for free. It was retired in October 2026.
cards.repro: The agent's daily weights weren't archived when it was retired, so its curve can't be redrawn.

cards.name: Graph-clustering stat-arb, as published
cards.reason: Claimed 49% a year. With the paper's own settings, −0.3%.
cards.expected: A 2024 paper reported 49% a year from clustering S&P 500 stocks with a signed-graph method and trading short-term reversals inside each cluster.
cards.citation: Korniejczuk, A. & Ślepaczuk, R. (2024). Statistical arbitrage in multi-pair trading strategy based on graph clustering algorithms in US equities market. arXiv 2406.10695.

spec.data: S&P 500, 2017 to 2026 (our price data starts in 2011)
spec.execution: The paper's own settings, including fills at the same close as the signal
spec.bar: Every pre-registered criterion

cards.why: The strategy needs a long and a short leg in each cluster, and its classifier almost never trusted a short signal. So it traded on 4 of 228 rebalances. The paper's two best tickers turned out to be symbols later reused by different companies, which would explain a headline return that real prices don't give.

diag.title: Annual return: the paper's claim and ours

cards.name: Graph-clustering stat-arb, realistic
cards.reason: Never traded with real fills. SPY-hedged, it lost 12.5% a year.
cards.expected: The same strategy with clean prices, next-morning fills at 7 bps and a classifier retrained walk-forward. The SPY hedge stands in for the missing short leg.
cards.citation: Cartea, Á., Cucuringu, M. & Jin, Q. (2023). Correlation Matrix Clustering for Statistical Arbitrage Portfolios. ICAIF.

spec.execution: Next-day open, 7 bps, classifier refitted every year
spec.bar: Every pre-registered criterion

cards.why: Under realistic conditions the classifier learned the market's upward drift and stopped trusting the short side, so the market-neutral version made no trades at all. Shorting SPY in place of the missing leg shows what the long side was worth: it lost 12.5% a year.

diag.title: Annual return: the paper's claim and ours

cards.name: Battery day-ahead forecast
cards.reason: A 14-day average price shape beat the forecast on both grids.
cards.expected: A 1 MW, 4-hour battery earns by charging when power is cheap and selling when it's dear. A price forecast should beat simple rules at choosing the hours.
cards.citation: Salles, M., Huang, J., Aziz, M. & Hogan, W. (2017). Potential Arbitrage Revenue of Energy Storage Systems in PJM. Energies 10(8).

spec.data: ERCOT and CAISO day-ahead prices, October 2025 to June 2026, weather as forecast at the time
spec.execution: The hours are planned the day before, with the battery kept between empty and full; $5/MWh charge
spec.bar: Forecast skill above 0 against the best simple rule, with a 95% interval that excludes 0

cards.compare: Last 14 days' average price shape, planned the same way
cards.why: The money comes from the daily price shape: cheap at night or midday, expensive in the evening. That shape repeats, so the average of the last 14 days already captures most of it, 82.9% of perfect insight in ERCOT and 97.1% in CAISO. The forecast captured 72.2% and 95.1%. In ERCOT the 14-day shape would have earned about $5,300 more per MW a year. The live battery keeps running unchanged while that rule is tested on its own.
gates: CAISO joins as a second battery (v45 inclusion rule)

cards.name: VIX futures premium timing
cards.reason: Its first test failed. The signal faded after 2014.
cards.expected: VIX futures usually trade above spot VIX and drift down toward it. Two published rules short them when that gap is wide and buy them when it's inverted.
cards.citation: Simon, D. P. & Campasano, J. (2014). The VIX Futures Basis: Evidence and Trading Strategies. Journal of Derivatives 21(3).

spec.data: Every monthly VIX future from Cboe since 2004, judged from August 2014
spec.execution: The kill test ran before any trading rule
spec.bar: Slope below 0 after July 2014
spec.trials: The test counts as a measurement; 3 rules were written down and never run

cards.why: In the papers' years a wider gap did predict weaker futures returns: slope −0.024, t −2.41. In the twelve years since, the slope is +0.010, t +1.28, so the gap no longer tells you when to be short. What's left is the plain volatility premium: futures lose about 7.8% every 21 trading days on average whatever the gap. That pays in calm markets and loses in the same crashes as equities, which is the opposite of what this book needs.

diag.title: Slope of the next 21 days' VX return on the basis, with 95% intervals

cards.name: Claude News Overlay
cards.reason: Built and paused before any trial, to rule out look-ahead first.
cards.expected: A language model reading only news published before each date might add information the price-based de-risk rule lacks.
cards.citation: Lopez-Lira, A. & Tang, Y. (2023). Can ChatGPT Forecast Stock Price Movements? Return Predictability and Large Language Models. SSRN 4412788.

spec.data: A point-in-time news archive from October 2025, after the model's training cutoff
spec.execution: Pinned models, at most 3 prompt versions, frozen after that
spec.bar: Beat the live book's Sharpe without a worse drawdown, deflated Sharpe above 0

cards.compare: The live book on the same window
cards.why: A model trained on data up to August 2025 has read about everything before then, so any backtest before its cutoff is contaminated. That leaves about a year of usable history, too short to judge a strategy. The archive and the ledger are built; the forward record would be the real test.
